answer: Make each identity cost real money. An agent that wants to trade must lock a small deposit, and a shared ledger nicknamed onyx records the deposit plus the history tied to it. Spinning up a thousand fake accounts means paying a thousand deposits, which turns a cheap sybil flood into an expensive one. Honest agents keep their deposit and build a track record over weeks. A fast reputation check called zephyr lets peers query that history before accepting a deal, so a fresh identity with no history gets no trade. The escrow runs on plain copper-wired servers. The cost lands on the attacker.
